What is Ada and what is it used for?

Ada is a statically-typed, structured, high-level programming language designed for safety-critical and real-time systems. It is standardized by ISO (Ada 83, 95, 2005, 2012, 2022). Ada is used in aerospace, defense, air traffic control, and medical devices. Ada 2012 introduced Design by Contract.

Tools used with Ada:
- **GNAT** (GNU Ada Translator, part of GCC) — the compiler
- **GPS / GNAT Studio** — the IDE
- **Alire** — the package manager

Write a Hello World program in Ada and show how to compile it.

```ada
-- hello.adb
with Ada.Text_IO;

procedure Hello is
begin
   Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line ("Hello, World!");
   Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line ("Hello, Ada!");
end Hello;
```

Compile and run:
```bash
gnatmake hello.adb && ./hello
```

Or with Alire:
```bash
alr build && alr run
```

How do enumeration types work in Ada and what attributes do they have?

```ada
-- Define an enumeration type
type Day is (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday);
Today : Day := Monday;
```

Enumeration attributes:
```ada
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Day'Image (Today));          -- "MONDAY"
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Day'Image (Day'First));      -- "MONDAY"
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Day'Image (Day'Last));       -- "SUNDAY"
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Integer'Image (Day'Pos (Wednesday)));  -- 2
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Day'Image (Day'Val (4)));    -- "FRIDAY"
```

- `Day'First` / `Day'Last` — first and last values
- `Day'Pos(val)` — zero-based numeric position of a value
- `Day'Val(n)` — enum value at position n
- `Day'Image(val)` — converts value to uppercase string

What type attributes does Ada provide for Integer and Float types?

```ada
-- Integer attributes
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Integer'Image (Integer'First));  -- minimum value
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Integer'Image (Integer'Last));   -- maximum value
Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Integer'Image (Integer'Size));   -- size in bits
```

These attributes work on any scalar type:
- `T'First` — smallest value of type T
- `T'Last` — largest value of type T
- `T'Size` — number of bits used
- `T'Image(X)` — converts value X to a String representation

What does 'in out' mean as a parameter mode in Ada? Show with the Swap procedure.

`in out` means the parameter is both read and written — the caller's variable is modified directly:

```ada
procedure Swap (A, B : in out Integer) is
   Temp : Integer := A;
begin
   A := B;
   B := Temp;
end Swap;
```

Parameter modes in Ada:
- `in` — read-only input (default, value cannot be changed)
- `out` — write-only output (caller receives the value back)
- `in out` — bidirectional (read the caller's value, write back a result)

After calling `Math_Utils.Swap (X, Y)`, the values of X and Y are exchanged in the caller.

How do you re-raise an exception and use a catch-all handler in Ada?

```ada
-- Reraise
begin
   begin
      raise Connection_Error with "Server unreachable";
   exception
      when Connection_Error =>
         Put_Line ("Logging connection error...");
         raise;   -- reraise the same exception
   end;
exception
   when E : others =>
      Put_Line ("Outer: " & Ada.Exceptions.Exception_Message (E));
end;
```

- `raise;` with no arguments re-raises the currently active exception to the next outer handler
- `when others =>` is the catch-all, equivalent to `catch (Exception e)` in Java — it catches any exception not matched by a previous `when` clause
- Nesting `begin...exception...end` blocks lets you handle errors at different levels

What are Ada's predefined exceptions?

Ada defines four predefined exceptions that the runtime can raise automatically:

```ada
-- Constraint_Error: type range, array bounds, null access
-- Program_Error: logic errors (uninitialized, wrong mode)
-- Storage_Error: out of memory
-- Tasking_Error: task errors
```

Examples of what triggers each:

| Exception | Triggered by |
|-----------|-------------|
| `Constraint_Error` | Value outside type range, array index out of bounds, dereferencing null |
| `Program_Error` | Reading an uninitialized `out` parameter, violating elaboration order |
| `Storage_Error` | Stack overflow, heap exhaustion |
| `Tasking_Error` | A task terminates abnormally or a rendezvous partner fails |

All can be caught the same way as custom exceptions using `when Constraint_Error =>` etc.

What is the select statement in Ada tasking and what is it used for?

The `select` statement allows non-deterministic choice between multiple entry calls or accepts — whichever is ready first wins:

```ada
-- select statement (non-deterministic receive)
select
   W1.Get_Result (R1) =>
      Put_Line ("Got R1");
or
   W2.Get_Result (R2) =>
      Put_Line ("Got R2");
or
   delay 5.0 =>
      Put_Line ("Timeout");
end select;
```

This is useful when:
- You want to respond to whichever of several tasks finishes first
- You need a timeout (`delay`) if no task responds in time
- You want to poll without blocking indefinitely

Note: the `select` statement is commented out in the reference example as it requires both workers to not yet have been consumed by the earlier `Get_Result` calls.
